about: Who sets prayer times in each country, and the method the app uses there. The single source for the iPhone, Android and web apps: run python3 tools/gen_countries.py after editing. source: table = the authority publishes a timetable the app downloads; authority = the app calculates with the authority's own published method; standard = no timetable the app can read, so a standard method (with the note saying which masjids differ). highLatitude: the rule for nights when twilight barely ends (angle = twilight angle portion, seventh = one seventh of the night, middle = middle of the night); left out, the method's own rule applies.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.note: There is no single national body for UK prayer times, and many masjids print their own. Many London masjids follow the London Unified Prayer Timetable. The app uses the Moonsighting Committee method, which was made for northern countries.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.note: Irish masjids publish their own timetables. The app uses the Moonsighting Committee method, made for northern countries.

countries.name: France
countries.note: France has no single body for prayer times. The Grande Mosquée de Paris uses 18°, Musulmans de France uses 12°. The app uses the Muslim World League method, which is close to 18°.

countries.name: Germany
